In the app, start a tour from Settings, Guide, from **Show me** on a page of the guide, or from the Help menu. Each step points at one part of the window; Escape ends the tour.

## Around the window

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

*For a wide window.*

1. Places in your vault. All items, favorites, one-time codes, the password generator, health checks and the trash. Which ones show, and in what order, is under Settings, Sidebar.
2. Search. Type part of a name, a website, a username or a tag. <kbd>Ctrl+F</kbd> (<kbd>⌘F</kbd> on a Mac) brings you here from anywhere in the window.
3. Add an item. Choose what kind it is: a login, a one-time code, a note, a card and more. <kbd>Ctrl+N</kbd> (<kbd>⌘N</kbd> on a Mac) adds the first kind on the menu.
4. Your items. Click one to see it. Right-click for the rest: copy, edit, favorite, pin, hide on the shelf or move to the trash.
5. Copy without showing it. These buttons copy the password or the username, or open the site. A copied secret is cleared from the clipboard after a while.
6. Lock. Locks the vault now. It also locks by itself after a while with nothing happening, which you can change under Settings, Security.
7. Settings and this guide. Every setting has a **?** beside it that says what it does. <kbd>F1</kbd> explains whatever you are looking at, and Settings, Guide has the rest.

## Around the window

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

*For a narrow window.*

1. Search. Type part of a name, a website, a username or a tag.
2. Add an item. Choose what kind it is: a login, a one-time code, a note, a card and more.
3. Your items. Click one to see it and copy from it. Right-click for the rest.
4. Pages. Your items, one-time codes, the generator and settings. Every setting has a **?** that says what it does.

## Around the app

*Only in Android.*

1. Search. Type part of a name, a website, a username or a tag.
2. Add an item. Choose what kind it is: a login, a one-time code, a note, a card and more.
3. Your items. Tap one to see it and copy from it. Swipe a row for a quick action, which you can choose under Settings, Appearance, Vault list.
4. Pages. Your items, one-time codes, the generator and health checks. Which ones show, and in what order, is under Settings, Appearance, Navigation.
5. Lock. Locks the vault now. It also locks by itself after you leave the app, which you can change under Settings, Security.
6. Settings and this guide. Every setting has a **?** beside it that says what it does, and Settings, Guide has the rest.

## Your first item

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

1. Every kind of item starts here. Logins, one-time codes, notes, cards, identities, Wi-Fi, SSH keys and more. This tour opens a new login for you.
2. Its name. What the item is called in your list. Leave it empty and the website’s name is used.
3. Username and password. Type them in, or generate a password from the button in its field. Nothing is saved until you save.
4. Everything else folds away. Websites, a one-time code, notes and more open when you need them. Which ones start open is under Settings, Editor.
5. Save. Saves the item to the vault. Close leaves without saving, and asks first if you changed anything.

## One-time codes

1. Every code in one place. Each item that has a one-time code is listed here. Click a code to copy it; double-click to open its item.
2. Add a code. Paste or scan the setup key a site shows when you turn on two-step sign-in, or bring your codes over from another app.

## The password generator

1. A new password. A fresh one each time something changes. Copy it, or save it as a new login.
2. What kind. Random characters, a few words, something you can say aloud, a PIN, or a pattern of your own.
3. Length and characters. Changes apply at once. What the generator starts with is under Settings, Generator.
4. Keep it. Starts a new login with this password already filled in.

## Health

1. The score. Out of 100: higher means fewer problems across your vault. It can be hidden under Settings, Health checks.
2. What to fix. Each group is one kind of problem, such as a password used more than once. Open a group to see its items and go to each one.

## Security settings

1. When the vault locks. After a time with nothing happening, when the computer sleeps, and what the clipboard keeps.
2. Your master password. Change it here. Rekeying also gives the vault a new key, so an old copy of the file cannot follow what you add later.
3. Ways in. Extra passwords, a key file or a security key. Each one opens the same vault.
4. If you are made to open it. Passwords that look ordinary at the door but erase, lock or open a decoy instead.
5. If you cannot open it. Split a recovery key between people you trust, so that enough of them together can get in.
6. Offline unless you say. Nothing leaves this device until this is on, and each network feature says what it sends.

## Backups

1. Where copies go. A folder, a WebDAV server, S3 storage or a cloud drive. A backup is the encrypted file itself, so only your password opens it.
2. How often, and how many. Copies can be made every day or every week while the app is running. The newest is checked before an older one is removed.
3. By hand. Save a copy as a file wherever you like, or merge in a file from elsewhere.

## Sync with another device

1. On the same network. Pair a phone or another computer once, by comparing a code. After that they sync directly, with nothing in between.
2. Through a folder or server. Use a place you already have for backups. Each device writes its own encrypted file there and merges the others.
3. Accounts held elsewhere. Open a Bitwarden account, your own server or a KeePass file alongside this vault.

## Browser extension

*Only in the desktop app.*

1. Let it connect. Turn this on, then **Set up browsers** so they can find WM Pass. The extension then uses the vault open here, so you unlock once.
2. Check the fingerprint. The first time an extension connects, it shows a fingerprint. It should match this one.
3. Connected extensions. Every extension that has connected. Forget one you no longer use.

## Quick search and auto-type

*Only in the desktop app.*

1. From anywhere. A shortcut that works in every program opens a small search window. Enter copies the password.
2. Typing for you. With this on, Shift+Enter in quick search types the username and password into the window that was in front.
